title: Story: Goldilocks and the three bears
summary: Goldilocks walks into the three bears' house, eats their porridge, breaks a chair and falls asleep in a bed. Very short sentences in the present tense, with a little Perfekt.
phrases: This chair is right for me.
Someone has eaten some of my porridge.
lines: Goldilocks and the three bears.
It's a beautiful morning.
In a small house in the forest live three bears:
Papa Bear, Mama Bear and their little son.
Mama Bear is making breakfast.
She is cooking porridge for the whole family.
But the porridge is still very hot.
Papa Bear looks at the porridge and says: "We can't eat it yet.
It's still too hot.
Let's wait a little.
Then we can eat the porridge.
In the meantime we can go for a walk outside."
"That's a good idea," says Mama Bear.
The three bears leave their house and go into the forest.
Meanwhile a little girl is walking through the forest.
The girl has long blond hair.
Her name is Goldilocks.
After a while Goldilocks sees a little house.
"I wonder who lives here?" she asks herself.
She goes to the house and knocks on the door.
But nobody answers.
Goldilocks waits a little and knocks again.
Again nobody answers.
The door is open.
Goldilocks looks inside and simply walks into the house.
On the table there are three bowls of porridge.
Goldilocks is hungry and tries the porridge from the first bowl.
Too hot!
Then she tries the second.
Too hot as well!
She tries the porridge from the third bowl.
Hmm … this one is good!
Goldilocks eats all the porridge.
She sees three chairs.
The first is too big.
The second is too big as well.
But the third is small.
"This chair is right for me."
Goldilocks sits down on it.
She wobbles back and forth a little.
Suddenly the little chair breaks.
"Oh no!" says Goldilocks.
After that she goes upstairs.
There are three beds there.
She tries the first and then the second bed.
Both are too big.
The third bed is small and cosy.
The bed is very comfortable.
Goldilocks lies down and quickly falls asleep.
After their walk the three bears come home.
Papa Bear looks at his porridge.
"Someone has eaten some of my porridge."
Mama Bear looks at her bowl.
"Someone has eaten some of my porridge too."
Baby Bear sees his empty bowl.
"Someone has eaten all my porridge!"
Then they see the chairs.
Papa Bear says: "Someone has been sitting on my chair."
Mama Bear says: "Someone has been sitting on my chair too."
Baby Bear looks at his little chair.
"Someone has broken my chair!"
The three bears go upstairs.
There they see Goldilocks in a bed.
Goldilocks wakes up and sees the three bears.
She gets very scared.
She jumps out of bed and runs downstairs as fast as she can.
She opens the door and runs out of the house.
The three bears don't run after her.
They stay in front of the house and watch Goldilocks go.
Goldilocks runs quickly through the forest.
She is still scared.
Papa Bear watches her go and says: "Now she knows she mustn't just walk into a stranger's house.
And she mustn't use other people's things."
Mama Bear nods. "That's right," she says.
Goldilocks runs on home.
Since that day she never goes into strangers' houses.
topics: Retell the story: who, where, what happens?
My breakfast: what do you eat in the morning?
My room: what is in your room?

focus.title: Too …
points: zu before an adjective means "too": zu heiß · zu groß
sehr just means "very" and isn't negative: sehr bequem (very comfortable)
Der Brei ist zu heiß → you can't eat it · Der Brei ist sehr heiß → it's just hot
The opposite: genau richtig = just right

focus.title: First, second, third
points: der erste · der zweite · der dritte — declined like adjectives
das erste Bett · die dritte Schüssel
After a preposition: aus der ersten Schüssel · aus der dritten Schüssel
From 4 on: vier → der vierte · zwanzig → der zwanzigste

focus.title: Spoken past (Perfekt)
points: haben + Partizip II: Jemand hat von meinem Brei gegessen.
sitzen → hat gesessen · machen → hat kaputt gemacht
The participle is always at the end: Jemand hat meinen Stuhl kaputt gemacht.
Verbs of movement use sein: Sie ist nach Hause gelaufen.

focus.title: Reflexive verbs
points: sich setzen: Goldlöckchen setzt sich darauf. (sits down)
sich hinlegen: Sie legt sich hin. (lies down)
sich fragen: „Wer wohnt hier?“, fragt sie sich.
The pronoun changes with the subject: ich setze mich · du setzt dich · sie setzt sich

focus.title: Allowed / not allowed
points: dürfen = to be allowed · nicht dürfen = must not, not allowed
Sie darf nicht einfach in ein fremdes Haus gehen.
Conjugation: ich darf · du darfst · er/sie darf · wir dürfen
The second verb goes to the end: Sie darf die Sachen nicht benutzen.
